EVERY AGE. THE SAME WORK.

Whānau-wide behaviour change starts with a shared language. Adults, teens and kids each have their own workbook — different depth, different words, same weekly theme — so the conversation keeps going in the car, at the dinner table, at bedtime.
Adults — A Reflective Workbook
A guided digital course book with live prompts, Q&A, and space to write into what the theme surfaces for you.
Teens — A Teen Workbook
Age-appropriate prompts and reflections in their own room — real language, real questions, no talking down.
Children — Colouring & Picture-book
Gentle activities and colouring pages built around the same weekly theme, so the little ones grow into the practice.
One wristband. One theme. One conversation the whole whānau can keep having.
IMAGE SLOT — a Mindcast wristband being tapped at the door (drag your image here; delete this line if none)
REFLECT. GATHER. COMMIT.
A cadence built around the only thing that actually changes behaviour — coming back next week and being asked whether you did it.
1 · Reflect on last week

Every session begins the same way — we return to the intention you set seven days ago. Did you do it? What got in the way? Where did the old pattern win? No shame, just honest data. This is the accountability loop most self-development is missing.
2 · This week's lesson

Adults, teens and kids move into their own rooms and work the same theme in parallel — live facilitation, workbook prompts, real conversation. The goal isn't more information. It's bringing the unconscious to the conscious.
3 · One intention. Actioned.

Before you leave, you write down one specific thing you'll do this week. It goes in your workbook, and it comes back with you next Sunday. That's how a room turns into a life. That's how a community changes.
A SPACE BUILT FOR FOLLOW-THROUGH
Every detail designed so Sunday gatherings and Tuesday Life Groups have a permanent, purpose-built home — theatre, breakout rooms, cafe, and a playground so parents can stay present.
